summary: New idiom: fəkle/foyək bala + poss.sf. mən 'jemanden in Ruhe lassen'

data.headword: fəkle/foyək bala + poss.sf. mən 'jemanden in Ruhe lassen'
data.turoyo: Hano məlle omər: "Bavo, gədyomeno, ḥatta d faykat u bala diḏux minan, aḥna lə ḥzelan mede.
data.translation: Der Gefährte antwortete: "Gut! Ich werde schwören, damit du uns endlich in Ruhe lässest. Wir haben nichts gefunden.

rationale: Searches bala, faykat, bala diḏ and bala min and the supplied fyk entry show no matching listed idiom. The trouble object and minan give the construction directly; one attestation.

summary: All six forms have the assigned stem and box: I fəkle with m-complement, I faykat/foyək, III mafəklux/gmafəkle, and III Detransitive mitafiko. Five tokens are already represented by inherited quotations.

I.1 alternates concrete loosening (chains) and intransitive desisting with m-. III.1 can release a confined participant or refuse release; the six tokens do not establish a clean causative distinction between I and III.
55/37 has overt u bala diḏux and minan rather than a simple patient “us”. Its noun-bound figurative result is placed in Idiomatic phrases; no sense number is added.
III Detransitive mitafiko presents the mare as affected subject and the key in b- as instrument, without an expressed agent. It is already cited and is not a new box.
No existing wording, numbering or examples have been rewritten.
Confirm the scope of bala + possessive + m- and the ay vowel in faykat at 55/37. Is this a conventional collocation beyond the single attestation?
Do speakers distinguish I and III release/loosening systematically, or do these tokens reflect lexical or dialectal overlap?
